converge-review-atomic.text: After the first partition rebalance, messages in thread-queue-parallel mode are dropped without being processed, and their offsets are still committed, causing silent data loss. The factory builds one FixedQueuePool in __init__ and hands it to every strategy. On revoke, close() and join() call queue_pool.shutdown(), but factory.queue_pool is not reset, so the next strategy's submit() reaches work_queue.put() which raises queue.ShutDown. The broad except then marks the offset complete and commits it.

The arroyo commit callback is called from the background _commit_loop thread instead of the consumer thread, racing with StreamProcessor's poll and rebalance handling. KafkaConsumer's staged-offset state is not thread-safe. On revoke, the commit thread is joined with only a 5s timeout, so it can still commit for a partition this consumer no longer owns. stage_offsets raises ConsumerError for unassigned partitions, which is swallowed by the except at :290.

There is no backpressure mechanism. The queues are unbounded (created with queue.Queue() and no maxsize) and submit() never raises MessageRejected, so memory grows without limit under consumer lag, contradicting the docstring's claim of 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up'. OffsetTracker all_offsets/outstanding also grow without limit.

On close/join, work already queued is abandoned. FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown = True before shutting down the queues, so each worker exits after its current item and does not drain its queue, defeating the immediate=False parameter.

close()/join() stop the commit thread without a final get_committable_offsets()/commit, so up to about 1s of completed work goes uncommitted on every revoke and graceful shutdown, breaking arroyo's join contract and causing at-least-once duplicates.
